Tigst Assefa won the 2025 London Marathon in 2:15:50, a women-only world record at the time, with Joyciline Jepkosgei second in 2:18:44 and Hassan falling back from the leaders around halfway.

Hassan skipped the 2025 World Championships to run the Sydney Marathon in August 2025, and by then had won the London, Chicago and Sydney majors.

Five berths per gender will be awarded via the FIBA 3x3 Federation Ranking based on standings as of 1 December 2027.

The first Federation Ranking of the new 24-month window had the Netherlands top of the combined table with USA, Spain and France close behind; the Netherlands led the women's ranking and Serbia led the men's.
At Paris 2024 the Netherlands beat France 18-17 in overtime for men's gold on a Worthy de Jong two-pointer, while Latvia won all seven pool games but lost to France in the semifinals.
At Paris 2024 Germany beat Spain 17-16 in the women's final for their first title, with Sonja Greinacher named MVP, and the United States took bronze.
Worthy de Jong said he considered retiring after Paris 2024 and has not committed to playing at the 2028 Games, though he expects the 2028 tournament to be the biggest yet.
Canada beat Azerbaijan 21-12 to win the 2025 FIBA 3x3 Women's Series Final in Shanghai on September 14, 2025, its third Women's Series title, with Saicha Grant-Allen named MVP.
The United States won the 2026 FIBA 3x3 World Cup women's title in Warsaw (June 1-7, 2026), its fourth World Cup crown, with Australia finishing runner-up.

facts: The organizing committee announced on May 8, 2025 that the 2028 Opening Ceremony will be held across two stadiums at the same time, the LA Memorial Coliseum in Exposition Park and SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, which no previous edition of the modern Games has done.
The official schedule lists the Opening Ceremony on Day 0, Friday, July 14, 2028, at 5:00 p.m. PT (8:00 p.m. ET).

SoFi Stadium will be called the 2028 Stadium (also referred to as the Stadium in Inglewood) during the Games; it opened in September 2020 and is home to the NFL's Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers.
SoFi Stadium will also host swimming during the 2028 Games, and the Games will be its first.
The LA Memorial Coliseum opened in 1923 and hosted the Opening Ceremonies of the 1932 and 1984 Summer Games, which makes 2028 its third Games.
In a Los Angeles City Council vote in November 2025 that moved the Closing Ceremony entirely to the Coliseum, the two-stadium plan for the Opening Ceremony was kept unchanged.

On October 28, 2026, organizers named film producer Kathleen Kennedy, former president of Lucasfilm, as Head of Ceremonies and Content; she will serve as an Executive Producer of the Opening and Closing Ceremonies.
Kennedy took over the role from Peter Rice, who stays on as an Executive Producer of the ceremonies after being named Netflix's Chief Content Officer in October 2026.
The ceremonies team also includes Ben Winston as Executive Producer and Creative Director, and longtime Games ceremonies producer Scott Givens as Executive Producer of Production.
Kennedy said that she and her husband, producer Frank Marshall, have attended almost every Games since Los Angeles 1984.
Official hospitality packages list the Opening Ceremony as session CER01A at 17:00 PT on Friday, July 14, 2028.
Reports from the 2025-2026 ticket sales said top Opening Ceremony seats went for more than $5,000 each, and ticket prices drew public complaints about cost.

facts: The official schedule lists the Closing Ceremony on Day 16, Sunday, July 30, 2028, at 6:00 p.m. PT (9:00 p.m. ET).

The Closing Ceremony was first planned to be split between the LA Memorial Coliseum and SoFi Stadium, but in November 2025 the Los Angeles City Council voted unanimously to hold it entirely at the Coliseum in Exposition Park.
Los Angeles Councilmember Marqueece Harris-Dawson said the change was meant to confirm the Coliseum as one of the only buildings in the world to host three Games opening or closing ceremonies.
The LA Memorial Coliseum opened in 1923, was built to attract the Games, and hosted the Opening Ceremonies of the 1932 and 1984 Summer Games.
The Coliseum will host both competition and ceremonies in 2028 and is expected to become the first venue to host events at three Summer Games.

On October 28, 2026, organizers named producer Kathleen Kennedy, former president of Lucasfilm, as Head of Ceremonies and Content, with responsibility for shaping the Games' farewell at the Closing Ceremony.

Peter Rice, Kennedy's predecessor and now Netflix's Chief Content Officer, stays on as an Executive Producer; Ben Winston is Executive Producer and Creative Director, and Scott Givens is Executive Producer of Production.
The Paralympic Closing Ceremony will also be held at the Coliseum, on August 27, 2028, after a Paralympic Opening Ceremony at the 2028 Stadium in Inglewood on August 15, 2028.

At the Paris 2024 Closing Ceremony, Los Angeles received the flag in a handover segment that included Tom Cruise and a pre-recorded Los Angeles program with Billie Eilish, Snoop Dogg and the Red Hot Chili Peppers.

facts: Etihad Park, a 25,000-seat soccer-specific stadium being built next to Citi Field at Willets Point in Queens, is the future home of New York City FC and was named a football venue for the 2028 Games on Feb. 3, 2026.

UEFA has three men's berths, decided at the 2027 UEFA European Under-21 Championship in Albania and Serbia from June 17 to July 4, 2027; Spain and France would need to qualify through that event.

At Paris 2024, men's squads were limited to under-23 players born on or after Jan. 1, 2001, with up to three overage players; the 2028 men's event is expected to keep a mostly under-23 format.

facts: The women's individual semifinal at the 2028 Games is scheduled for Saturday, July 15, 2028, 9:00-13:30 Pacific Time at Valley Complex 2 in the Valley Zone, formerly called the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area, in the San Fernando Valley.
Modern pentathlon opens the 2028 Games program, holding the first four days of competition (July 15-18) for the first time since 1992, with women's and men's semifinals on the first two days.
Under the new format, each semifinal and final has 18 athletes and runs in this order: direct-elimination fencing, then obstacle, then swimming, then the laser run.
In the obstacle discipline, athletes race head-to-head over a 70m course with eight obstacles, and it replaces the horse riding last used at Paris 2024.
Michelle Gulyas (HUN) won gold at Paris 2024, ahead of Elodie Clouvel (FRA) with silver and Seong Seung-Min (KOR) with bronze.
Egypt's Farida Khalil, aged 14 in 2025, won the 2025 senior world title in Kaunas, Lithuania, and also won world titles at Junior (U22), U19 and U17 level that year.
Before the 2025 World Championships, UIPM described Khalil as world No.1 and world record-holder, and she won the 2025 World Cup Final in Alexandria, Egypt.
Blanka Guzi (HUN), fourth at Paris 2024, won a second straight world silver medal in 2025, and Aurora Tognetti (ITA) took bronze.
Gulyas won the 2025 World Cup in Budapest on home soil in April 2025 but missed the 2025 World Championships because she had not recovered from an injury.

Other women expected to contend, based on 2025 form, include France's Rebecca Castaudi, the 2025 European champion, Hungary's Blanka Bauer and Seong Seung-Min, who was reigning world champion going into 2025.

facts: The 2028 Games mountain bike races will be held at the Industry Hills MTB Course in the City of Industry, Los Angeles County, next to the Pacific Palms Resort, after organizers moved the venue from Bonelli Park in San Dimas.

Organizers describe the Industry Hills course as set in the hills of the San Gabriel Valley with technical sections including drops and jumps, plus spectator areas close to the action; exact route length and elevation profile had not been published as of the 2025 announcement.

Tom Pidcock (GBR), gold medalist at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, won the 2026 men's elite XCO world title in Val di Sole, starting 35th on the grid and finishing ahead of fellow Briton Charlie Aldridge, his second XCO world title after 2023.
Pidcock won the 2026 world title after finishing ninth overall at the 2026 Tour de France, and he had raced his mountain bike only once that year before the championships.

After the 2026 world championships, Pidcock said he would focus on road racing in 2027 and return to mountain biking before the 2028 Games, where he would be going for a third consecutive gold in the event.

Alan Hatherly (RSA), Paris 2024 bronze medalist, won back-to-back XCO world titles in 2024 and 2025; in 2025 at Crans-Montana, Switzerland, he won in 1:30:30, 48 seconds ahead of Simone Avondetto (ITA) and 51 seconds ahead of Victor Koretzky (FRA).
Hatherly joined the road team Jayco-AlUla in 2025 and said combining road and mountain bike racing that season was difficult, with the world title defense a major goal.
Victor Koretzky (FRA), Paris 2024 silver medalist, won the short track (XCC) world title and took XCO bronze at the 2025 world championships.

Christopher Blevins (USA) won both the 2025 XCO and XCC World Cup overall titles, finishing the XCO series with 1996 points ahead of Martín Vidaurre Kossmann (CHI) on 1695 and Luca Martin (FRA) on 1546.
Pinkbike readers noted Blevins was the first American man to win the XCO World Cup overall since John Tomac, a storyline for a home-soil race at the 2028 Games.
Charlie Aldridge (GBR) won the 2025 World Cup finale at Mont-Sainte-Anne and was runner-up to Pidcock at the 2026 world championships.
Ten-time world champion Nino Schurter (SUI) rode his final world championships in 2025, finishing 42nd, and Mathieu van der Poel (NED) finished 29th in that race.

facts: The women's 10km at the 2028 Games is scheduled for July 17 at Belmont Shore in Long Beach, California, raced in the Pacific Ocean, with the men's race the following day.

The 2028 field is capped at 22 athletes, and the main qualification routes are the 2027 World Aquatics Championships in Budapest (open water July 4-8, 2027), the open water world ranking in February 2028, and a 2028 qualification event.

The top three finishers in the women's 10km at the 2027 World Aquatics Championships in Budapest earn places at the 2028 Games, and the remaining spots are decided at a qualification event planned for spring 2028.
Paris 2024 champion Sharon van Rouwendaal of the Netherlands announced her retirement on September 5, 2025, at age 31, so she will not defend her title in 2028.
Van Rouwendaal retired as the only swimmer to win two gold medals in the 10km (2016 and 2024), and she also took silver at Tokyo 2020.
Paris 2024 silver medalist Moesha Johnson of Australia won the women's 10km at the 2025 World Aquatics Championships in Singapore in 2:07:51.3, the first world 10km title ever won by an Australian.
Johnson also won the 5km and took bronze in the 3km knockout sprint in Singapore, and SwimSwam reported she finished 2025 ranked No. 1.
World Aquatics named Johnson its 2025 female Open Water Swimmer of the Year.
Paris 2024 bronze medalist Ginevra Taddeucci of Italy took silver in both the 10km and the 5km at the 2025 World Championships, finishing about 4.4 seconds behind Johnson in the 10km.
Monaco's Lisa Pou won bronze in the 2025 world 10km, Monaco's first ever medal at a World Aquatics Championships.
Taddeucci won the 2025 World Cup overall women's title after winning the final 10km stop in Golfo Aranci, Italy, in October 2025.
Johnson and Taddeucci went one-two at the 2025 World Cup opener in Soma Bay, Egypt, finishing 16 seconds clear of third place, which continued a rivalry from their Paris podium.
The 2025 world 10km races in Singapore were postponed because of poor water quality off Sentosa, so water conditions remain a storyline for ocean venues.
Johnson and Taddeucci are projected to contend in 2028 based on their 2025 form, but neither has qualified yet.

facts: The men's 10km at the 2028 Games is scheduled for July 18 at Belmont Shore in Long Beach, California, raced in the Pacific Ocean, one day after the women's race.

The 2028 field is capped at 22 athletes, and the main qualification routes are the 2027 World Aquatics Championships in Budapest (open water July 4-8, 2027), the open water world ranking in February 2028, and a 2028 qualification event.

The top three in the men's 10km at the 2027 World Aquatics Championships in Budapest earn places at the 2028 Games, and the remaining spots are decided at a qualification event planned for spring 2028.

Germany's Florian Wellbrock won the men's 10km at the 2025 World Aquatics Championships in Singapore, holding off a late charge from Italy's Gregorio Paltrinieri, with Australia's Kyle Lee taking bronze.
Wellbrock's 2025 win made him the first swimmer to win three world titles in the 10km, and it was his seventh world title in open water.
Wellbrock won the 10km at Tokyo 2020, and World Aquatics named him its 2025 male Open Water Swimmer of the Year.
The 2025 silver gave Paltrinieri his 17th World Championships medal, and the bronze was Kyle Lee's first individual medal at an international event.
Paris 2024 champion Kristof Rasovszky of Hungary and his teammate, bronze medalist David Betlehem, were among the pre-race favorites in Singapore in 2025 but did not reach the podium.
Rasovszky won the first European 3km knockout sprint title at the 2025 European Open Water Championships in Stari Grad, Croatia.
Paris 2024 silver medalist Oliver Klemet of Germany was listed among the top contenders before the 2025 world 10km.
The 2025 world 10km races in Singapore were postponed because of poor water quality, and Wellbrock described the conditions as very warm water.
Wellbrock and Paltrinieri are projected to contend in 2028 based on their 2025 form, but neither has confirmed participation or qualified.

facts: Beach sprint coastal rowing at the 2028 Games is held along Belmont Shore in Long Beach on July 24-25, 2028.
The 2028 Games will be the first time a rowing event at the Games is raced on the ocean.
The 2028 Games allocate 64 of rowing's 502 quota places to beach sprints, and each nation can qualify at most one male and one female athlete.
The main qualification event is the 2027 World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals in Oeiras, Portugal, scheduled for 6-9 October 2027, along with continental qualification events.
A beach sprint race includes a run up the sand, a 250m slalom row with two buoys, a 180-degree turn around a final buoy and a row back to shore before a run to the finish.
At the 2026 World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals in Qingdao, Moritz Wolff (GER) set the fastest men's solo time trial, 3.3 seconds ahead of defending champion Chris Bak (USA).
At the 2026 world finals in Qingdao, Isabella Scammell (AUS) won the women's solo time trial 1 by seven seconds over Raminta Morkunaite (LTU) and Zhu Wenjie (CHN), with Magdalena Lobnig (AUT) fourth.

At the 2025 world finals in Antalya, Wolff was fastest in the men's solo time trials and Emma Twigg (New Zealand) posted the fastest women's time, while defending champions Bak and Lobnig also advanced to the knockouts.
The 2026 time trials in Qingdao were run in difficult surf, with many capsizes, after storms cancelled training and competition over the opening weekend.
The men's solo at the 2026 world finals drew 48 entries, the largest men's solo field in World Rowing beach sprint history.
Samuel Forbes (AUS) was seventh in the 2026 time trials and went on to win men's solo silver, which shows that a seeding position from the time trials does not decide the knockouts.

facts: Chris Bak (USA) won the men's solo at the World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals in 2024 and 2025 and is a four-time beach sprint world champion.
After the 2025 world finals, Bak had six World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals medals (four gold, one silver, one bronze), and nobody has won more gold medals.
Bak won the first-ever US beach sprint gold in the men's solo in 2022 in Saundersfoot, Wales.
At the 2026 world finals in Qingdao, 21-year-old Liu Jiayu (CHN) won the men's solo ahead of 20-year-old Samuel Forbes (AUS), and Moritz Wolff (GER) took bronze over Allison Russo (POR).
Liu Jiayu overcame an equipment failure in the 2026 final when his boat's sliding seat came loose, and he won China's first men's solo world title.
On the way to the 2026 final, Forbes knocked out Bak in the quarterfinals, and Liu beat European champion Ander Martin (ESP).
At the 2025 world finals, Bak beat Ander Martin (ESP) in the men's solo final, after Wolff tripped and fell on the beach run in his semifinal against Martin.
Isabella Scammell (AUS) won the 2026 women's solo world title ahead of Zhu Wenjie (CHN), which was Australia's first gold at any Beach Sprint Finals.
Magdalena Lobnig (AUT) won women's solo bronze in 2026, after gold in 2024 and silver in 2025, and has reached the podium three years in a row.
In the 2026 women's solo knockouts, Christine Cavallo (USA) missed the buzzer in her quarterfinal against Scammell, and Lobnig went the wrong way around a slalom buoy in her semifinal.
None of these athletes has been confirmed for the 2028 Games, because quota places will be decided mainly at the 2027 world finals in Oeiras, Portugal.

facts: The 2028 Games shotgun events will be held at Whittier Narrows Clay Shooting Center in South El Monte, within the Whittier Narrows Recreation Area, while rifle and pistol events go to the Long Beach Target Shooting Hall.
Under the ISSF 2026 Rulebook, skeet finals now take eight athletes instead of six, so the top eight from qualification advance to the final.
The new eight-athlete skeet final format was tested at the 2025 ISSF World Cup Final in Doha, and the rules took effect on January 1, 2026.
Vincent Hancock (USA) won Paris 2024 men's skeet gold, his fourth in the event, and has said he intends to go for a fifth men's skeet gold at the 2028 Games.
Hancock won his fifth world title in men's skeet at the 2025 ISSF World Championship Shotgun in Athens, and the USA (Hancock, Conner Prince, Christian Elliott) also won the men's skeet team title.
Samantha Simonton (USA) won her first world title in women's skeet at Athens 2025 with 57, ahead of Mexico's Gabriela Rodriguez (54) and Sweden's Victoria Larsson.
At the 2025 ISSF World Cup Final in Doha, Christian Elliott won men's skeet ahead of Hancock and Dustan Taylor, so Americans took all three men's skeet medals.
At the 2025 ISSF World Cup Final, China's Jiang Yiting won women's skeet ahead of Simonton and Greece's Emmanouela Katzouraki.
ISSF reported that all three U.S. women's skeet athletes, Kimberly Rhode, Samantha Simonton and Dania Vizzi, won ISSF World Cup gold medals in 2025.
Francisca Crovetto (CHI) is the reigning Paris 2024 women's skeet champion, with Amber Rutter (GBR) silver and Austen Smith (USA) bronze.
The first skeet quota places for the 2028 Games are scheduled to be awarded on November 6, 2026 at the ISSF World Championship in Doha, three each for men and women.

ISSF has confirmed that in the 10m air rifle, 10m air pistol and trap mixed team events at the 2028 Games, the top four qualifying teams go straight into one medal final.
The new mixed team format replaces the separate gold and bronze medal matches used at Paris 2024, and the four finalist teams now compete together using an elimination format.

France's silver-medal team in Hamburg in 2025 was Léonie Périault, Yanis Seguin, Cassandre Beaugrand and Dorian Coninx; Germany's bronze-medal team was Tertsch, Lasse Nygaard Priester, Tanja Neubert and Henry Graf.

No 2028 rosters have been confirmed; qualification is ongoing.
Sweden's David Ahman and Jonatan Hellvig, the Paris 2024 men's champions, won the 2025 FIVB World Championship in Adelaide in November 2025.
Ahman and Hellvig became the youngest beach volleyball world champions ever at ages 23 and 24, according to Games-organizer coverage of the Adelaide final.
Ahman said after the 2025 world title that the pair had not expected to win in Adelaide because he had been injured.
Brazil's Ana Patricia and Duda, the Paris 2024 women's champions, lost in the Round of 16 at the 2025 World Championship to Americans Donlin and Denaburg, 2-0.
Latvia's Tina Graudina and Anastasija Samoilova won the 2025 women's world title, beating Americans Kristen Nuss and Taryn Brasher 21-15, 15-21, 15-11 in the final.
Latvia's 2025 title was the country's first men's or women's podium finish at a beach volleyball World Championship.
The U.S. teams will play at home in Southern California, where the sport is deeply rooted.

facts: Beach volleyball at the 2028 Games will be held at Alamitos Beach in Long Beach, a site announced in 2025 after Santa Monica was dropped as the planned venue.
Long Beach is set to host at least 11 sports during the 2028 Games, more than any venue city other than Los Angeles.
Under the FIVB qualification system announced December 11, 2025, 48 teams (24 men's and 24 women's) will qualify for the 2028 beach volleyball tournaments.
The USA, as host nation, gets one guaranteed quota place per gender and can earn a second through the standard qualification pathways.

Quota places come from the 2026 Continental Championships or Continental Tour Finals, the 2027 World Championships in the Netherlands (one place per gender for the winners), and the ranking list, which closes in 2028 and provides most of the places.
Sweden's Jacob Holting Nilsson and Elmer Andersson won the 2026 CEV EuroBeachVolley men's title over Norway's Anders Mol and Christian Sorum, earning Sweden a 2028 quota place.
The Netherlands' Schoon and Stam won the 2026 European women's title, securing a Dutch women's quota place.
Australia won both 2026 AVC Continental Championship titles in Shangluo, China: Mark Nicolaidis and Izac Carracher for the men and Stefanie Fejes and Taliqua Clancy for the women.

Morocco's men (Zouheir Elgraoui and Soufiane El Gharouti) and Nigeria's women (Esther Onyinye Mbah and Pamela Miyoum Bawa) won the 2026 CAVB African titles, making them the first African beach volleyball teams to earn quotas for the Games.
At the 2025 World Championships in Adelaide, the quarterfinals included an all-American match between Kristen Nuss/Taryn Brasher and Julia Donlin/Lexy Denaburg.
As of late 2026, no team rosters for the 2028 Games have been finalized, so Round of 16 matchups are unknown.

facts: This session is a women's preliminary-round match at Honda Center; volleyball at the 2028 Games is scheduled for 15-30 July 2028.
On 11 December 2025 the FIVB announced the qualification system for the 2028 Games volleyball tournaments.
Under the FIVB system, the last three places in each tournament go by FIVB World Ranking after the preliminary round of the 2028 Volleyball Nations League.
Each women's tournament has 12 teams, with the host United States holding one automatic place.
At Paris 2024, Italy won its first women's gold by sweeping the United States 3-0, and Brazil won bronze.
Italy won the 2025 Women's Volleyball Nations League, beating Brazil 3-1 (22-25, 25-18, 25-22, 25-22) in the final in Lodz, Poland, on 27 July 2025.
The 2025 title was Italy's third Nations League crown, and it kept the title it won in 2024.
Brazil's Gabriela Guimaraes and Italy's Myriam Sylla were named best outside hitters at the 2025 Women's Nations League.
Italy opposite Paola Egonu, MVP at Paris 2024, was born 18 December 1998 and captained Vero Volley Milano in 2026.
